The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Kiran M.S., in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.09.2018.
2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:

On 01.09.2018 at about 4.45 a.m. the deceased Kiran was proceeding in a DTDC company attached  3 SCCH-17 MVC 7828/2018 canter lorry bearing No. KA-02-AG-1499 belonging to first respondent which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the ahead going lorry.

Due to the impact,
the deceased who was traveling in the cabin of the canter lorry suffered severe fatal injuries and died on the spot.

At the time of accident, the deceased was working as Incharge writer at DTDC Courier Maxi Vendor and he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month and he was contributing the same to his family maintenance but due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically.
The petitioners have lost love and affection and care taker.

In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.

In tort law,

13 . In the accident cases the concept of Res ipsa loquitur which means the thing speaks for itself plays very important role on the point of adjudication of negligence in the accident cases.
In the context of a legal claim based on negligence, res ipsa loquitur essentially means that the circumstances surrounding the case make it obvious that negligence occurred.

The improper admission  or rejection of evidence  shall not be ground of  itself for a new trial or  reversal of any decision  in any case, if it shall  appear to the court  before which such  objection is raised that,
